rule_metadata.description: The complete merging of Noon Sakinah or Tanween into the letters Ra (ر) or Lam (ل) without any remaining nasal resonance.

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Complete insertion of the sound of Noon Sakinah or Tanween into the succeeding letter so that no trace of the Noon remains.
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: When a non-vowelled Noon (نْ) or Tanween is followed by either Ra (ر) or Lam (ل) across two words, the Noon converts entirely into the destination letter with Tashdeed, and the Ghunnah (nasal sound) is completely eliminated.

trigger_letters.name: Lam
trigger_letters.reason: The articulation point and attributes of Noon merge completely into Lam.

trigger_letters.name: Ra
trigger_letters.reason: The articulation point and attributes of Noon merge completely into Ra.

theoretical_foundation.acoustic_rule: No nasal resonance (Ghunnah) from Al-Khayshum should be heard. The sound transitions immediately from the preceding vowel to the doubled Lam or Ra.

special_quranic_exception.rule: Sakt (Obligatory Brief Pause) in Surah Al-Qiyamah
special_quranic_exception.explanation: Because of the obligatory pause (Sakt) on the word 'مَنْ', Idgham is NOT performed here. The Noon Sakinah is read clearly (Izhar) with a brief breath-holding pause before 'رَاقٍ'.

practical_examples.breakdown: The Noon Sakinah merges completely into Lam. No nasal sound is held.
The Noon Sakinah merges completely into Ra with Tashdeed. The Ra retains its heavy pronunciation without any nasal hum.
The Tanween on Hudan merges into the Lam of Lil-muttaqeen without Ghunnah.
The Tanween merges directly into the heavy Ra without nasalization.
